Independent determinant and rank check for W_{2,3}(5)
correctness.rationale: The displayed structure constants define the Lie ring on the free Z-module with the stated basis (not a free Lie algebra on generators). The alternating CE differential sends X_i to −T∧Y_i and is zero on the T-containing summand. Thus H^j splits into the degree-j kernel and the degree-(j−1) cokernel of the derivation. In characteristic two this derivation squares to zero and factors as a tensor differential; each pair contributes homology in exterior degrees 0 and 2, giving H_δ=(1+q²)^r(1+q)^s. The kernel dimensions are half the sum of the exterior and δ-homology dimensions, yielding (1). The torsion of the integral cokernel survives unchanged in CE cohomology, and the difference of rational and F₂ ranks counts exactly the even Smith factors. For the rational kernel one can also group by singly occupied pairs and sum the middle binomial coefficients of their Boolean lattices, giving the characteristic-zero profile cited in the record. Multiplication by (1+q)^s and a one-degree shift give (2), and Vandermonde gives (3). For r≥3 the three-singly-occupied-pair block already has a 3×3 minor of determinant ±2 on its isolated middle map, yielding a rank drop in that block. The r=3 and r=4 examples agree with the profiles. An independent W_{2,3}(5) test gave determinant −48 and ranks 6 and 9 in characteristics 2 and 3, as expected from its diagonal form; this is not a full-complex replay.
residual_risks: Read 'free integral Lie ring with the identical basis and structure constants' as the explicitly prescribed Lie ring free as a Z-module. Neither (2) nor the frozen check script establishes individual Smith exponents in general.

evidence: The older Lie-cohomology results give the characteristic-zero length-two case but do not give modular or integral information.

Wilson's t,k-subset result over Z yields a diagonal with entries binom(k−i,t−i) of multiplicity binom(n,i)−binom(n,i−1) in the range t≤min(k,n−k). An adjacent-level block outside that range can be complemented and transposed to put it in range.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The integral theorem on the actual constituent matrices is stronger than the claimed rank decrement and covers every block, including blocks of unequal row and column sizes. No extension from a characteristic-zero Lie result to characteristic two is needed.

evidence: For fixed m=|S| and X layer a, take j=min(a,m−a+1); after complement/transpose if needed the entries are j−i for i=0,…,j−1 with known binomial-difference multiplicities. Counting those divisible by 2 yields exactly the summands counted in (2), and rank modulo 2 gives (1); the same entries give all primary exponents after taking their prime-power parts.
For W_{2,3}(5) the entries are 3, four copies of 2, and five copies of 1, matching the independent check and displaying integral information stronger than the claimed parity profile.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The rank difference and graded sum use only the CE splitting and a standard direct-sum basis organization. Expressing those ranks with compact generating polynomials does not escape the stronger theorem.

RESULT.md Proof, integral differential and rank difference

evidence: Fix the fully occupied pairs, the singly occupied pairs S and the selected Z variables in a monomial basis ordered by pair. A subset A of S records the X positions. Replacing one X by its Y produces A minus that position with coefficient +1; degree-zero derivation and pair ordering give no signs.

The map from the a-X layer to the (a−1)-X layer is W_{a−1,a}(|S|), up to transpose/index convention. Distinct layers have disjoint domain and image summands, so the full differential is their integral direct sum with zero summands.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is exact integral equivalence by basis permutations, not an analogy between ranks or a similarity in title.

originality.rationale: The prior integral Boolean inclusion diagonal form covers all the nonzero component maps of the frozen CE differential exactly. The finite-characteristic Betti and even-order rank profiles are mechanical graded counts from those same diagonal forms; they are not new exact facts independent of that stronger result. This assessment is based on an explicit integral block identification and a verified statement of Wilson's theorem, not on absence of direct matches or failure to retrieve Wilson's own copy.

value.rationale: The Lie family is natural, but the claimed new finite-characteristic and integral invariants are rank projections of already diagonalized integer maps, with no new rank determination required after the standard decomposition. A convenient two-primary rank summary does not supply an independent new invariant result; even the torsion orders omitted by this record are available blockwise from the older form. There is no distinct valuable remainder in the submitted claim to repair.
residual_risks: This assessment does not address a different claim about the multiplicative structure of cohomology or actions with longer Jordan blocks.
